Using both destructive sectioning and ultrasonic non-destructive testing across a sample of 32 previously manufactured shafts, they found the rejections traced to alumina/oxide-type non-metallic inclusions that caused surface and sub-surface cracking. The root cause analysis pointed specifically to the refractory lining, the furnace hot-top, and the ladle as the significant contamination sources — and the corrective fix was replacing the low-quality flux and refractory lining material with standardized, higher-quality alternatives.

This study characterizes different types of rolled-in scale defects on hot-rolled steel strip by appearance, the grades most prone to each type, and metallographic examination. It explains the underlying mechanism: oxide scale forms on the strip surface in the reheating furnace before rolling due to high-temperature oxidation, and is normally removed by hydraulic descaling during the hot rolling operation; when the primary scale is not fully removed by the descaler, it gets pressed (rolled) into the surface, which is specifically termed 'rolled-in scale.' The paper ties each characterized scale type back to a specific root cause and matching remedial action.

The authors note that defect detection and root cause analysis in hot strip mills is largely a manual process today, which makes it vulnerable to human error, delayed feedback, and knock-on effects across successive steel products further down the line. They propose combining expert domain knowledge with machine learning models specifically for width-related defects, arguing that automated RCA tools remain rare outside of surface-defect image detection and roller-force optimization, leaving a real gap between defect detection and actually explaining why a defect occurred.

This paper studies fold defects in die forging, which occur when the workpiece undergoes complex material flow inside die cavities and improper processing conditions cause the metal surface to overlap onto itself rather than bond. The authors classify folding defects into three distinct types based on the material flow pattern that produces them: confluence-type (two flow fronts meeting and folding over each other), bending-type (the wall of a cavity bending back on itself), and local-loading-type (uneven local deformation concentrating flow into a fold). They demonstrate the approach on a real axially-symmetric flanged steel component, where folding is strongly tied to the part's geometrical parameters (billet shape, die shape) rather than being a single generic cause.

This case study examines a real production problem: a multi-directional die-forged valve body where, under the unoptimized process in use, nearly all forged parts showed fold defects, with over half being severe enough to cause substantial financial loss. Using finite-element modeling, the authors systematically varied billet initial temperature, punch speed, and billet-die friction coefficient to identify which process parameters most strongly drove fold formation, then used those findings to redesign the process rather than the die itself.

This study investigates surface deterioration of high-chromium roll steel (the work rolls used in hot rolling) caused by thermal fatigue. Using a laboratory test replicating real hot-rolling thermal cycling, samples were cycled up to 4,500 times at temperatures of 500, 600, and 700C followed by water cooling, with periodic sectioning to examine microstructure and crack development. The authors found that repeated thermal cycling causes oxidation-assisted crack growth that eventually leads to spalling (surface particles breaking away), and that the specific combination of temperature, chemical composition, and thermal stress determines how and where cracking initiates and propagates.

This review paper discusses why steel surface defects matter beyond appearance: crazing can cause rupture, inclusions affect the internal stress state of steel structures, and patches and pitted surface specifically affect resistance to wear and corrosion. It also distinguishes microstructural defects (linked to deoxidation and segregation during steelmaking, producing non-metallic inclusions or microcracks) from purely surface-level defects, and notes that even very small defects (under 100 micrometers) can be detrimental to fatigue strength in high-strength steel grades, though the critical size threshold depends on the specific steel grade.

This is a real Tata Steel R&D paper studying 'tong mark' defects — surface marks left on Interstitial-Free (IF) steel coils by the mechanical tongs/grippers used to handle coils during loading into and out of the batch annealing furnace (BAF), a process step needed to restore formability after cold rolling. Note: full findings text was not fully retrievable from the available source snippet, so treat this citation as confirming the real topic, authorship, and venue (a genuine Tata Steel technical study, exactly matching the dossier's own suggested 'Tata Steel / SAIL public technical notes' bonus source) rather than as a source for specific quantitative claims — cite the original conference paper directly if you need exact findings.

This paper studies 'roll marks' — a related defect family to scratches — which occur periodically and over large areas on hot-rolled steel strip, and are considered one of the most serious defect categories by steel mills specifically because a single damaged or cracked roll surface repeats its mark on every subsequent rotation, turning a single root cause (roll surface damage) into a large-area, continuously recurring defect pattern rather than an isolated scratch.
Crazing. A network of fine, shallow surface cracks that form on the strip surface, typically linked to thermal stress or repeated stress cycling during hot deformation.

Inclusion. Foreign non-metallic particles (oxides, slag, refractory fragments) trapped inside the steel matrix during solidification. Some inclusions are loosely bound and flake off at the surface; others remain pressed into the material and only appear after rolling exposes them.

Patches. A localized region of the strip surface visually distinguished from the surrounding material by a particular characteristic (texture, reflectivity, or color), usually from uneven descaling or oxide formation.

Pitted Surface / Rolled Pit. A localized corrosion or mechanical-indentation pattern concentrated on a small area of the surface, penetrating into the material interior. Often linked to descaling effectiveness or roll-surface condition.
Rolled-in Scale. Oxide scale that was not fully removed before rolling gets pressed into the strip surface during the rolling pass, leaving an embedded scale pattern rather than a clean surface.
Scratches. Linear surface marks (horizontal, vertical, or slanting) from mechanical contact with equipment, rollers, or handling surfaces during transport or finishing operations.
Crescent Gap. A half-circle-shaped material loss defect that occurs during shearing/cutting of the strip, typically from blade wear or misalignment in the cutting station.
Waist Folding. Visible folds/wrinkles from excessive local deformation, generally associated with low-carbon material behavior under forming stress or die-fill issues.

Weld Line Defect. A defect at the coil-to-coil weld joint (used when splicing strip ends for continuous processing); while a weld line itself is a normal process feature, a defective weld shows incomplete fusion, offset, or thickness variation that must be tracked and diverted downstream.

Water Spot / Oil Spot. Low-contrast surface staining from residual moisture (drying step) or lubricant/coolant residue not fully removed during finishing. Easily confused with each other due to similar low-contrast appearance.

ISO 9001:2015 clause 10.2.1 Nonconformity and corrective action. When a nonconformity occurs (including one arising from a complaint), the organization must react to it, take action to control and correct it, deal with the consequences, and then evaluate whether action is needed to eliminate the root cause(s) so the nonconformity does not recur or occur elsewhere — including reviewing and analyzing the nonconformity, determining its causes, and checking whether similar nonconformities exist or could occur in other areas.

ISO 9001:2015 clause 10.2.2 Documentation of corrective action. The organization must retain documented evidence of the nature of the nonconformity and any subsequent action taken, and of the results of any corrective action, and must review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken.

IATF 16949:2016 clause 10.2.3 Problem solving. Extends ISO 9001 10.2 with automotive-sector requirements: the organization must have a documented process for problem solving that includes containment, root cause analysis and its verification, implementation of systemic corrective actions, verification of the effectiveness of these actions, and review/update of the relevant documentation (FMEAs, control plans) as needed.

IATF 16949:2016 clause 10.2.4 Error-proofing. Requires the organization to apply error-proofing methods, appropriate to the severity of the problem, as part of the corrective action process — i.e., the preventive action should where possible make recurrence physically or procedurally difficult, not just rely on inspection or training alone.

Latham and Giannetti describe a tool combining expert knowledge with machine learning to detect and investigate width-related defects in hot rolling. Their abstract reports training and validation with data from an operating mill. This is a general research reference, not a record of the current investigation, and it does not supply diagnostic test costs or outcome likelihoods for this application.

initial_information.value: Fine surface crack network observed on hot-rolled coil HR-1187, Line 1, concentrated in the mid-width region. Approximately 3% of coils in the shift showed the pattern under inspection light.

established_cause.value: The furnace maintenance test procedure has no mandatory step requiring verification that temperature control is returned to automatic mode before the furnace is released back to production.

value: Return zone-3 controller to automatic mode immediately; re-inspect all coils processed during the override window for crazing before release.

Add a mandatory 'return-to-auto' checklist item with technician and shift-supervisor dual sign-off to the furnace maintenance test work instruction; interlock the furnace HMI to alarm if manual override remains active beyond 30 minutes.

initial_information.value: Operator on Line 3 night shift flagged crazing on the trailing end of coil HR-1340, roughly 1.5m of affected length, first noticed on the 6th coil of a new steel grade changeover.

established_cause.value: The changeover checklist does not list run-out table cooling recipe verification as its own explicit item, so it gets silently skipped under the assumption it's covered elsewhere.

value: Load the correct cooling recipe immediately; quarantine and inspect all coils since changeover start for crazing.
Split the changeover checklist's 'verify rolling parameters' item into separate, individually-signed sub-items, with 'run-out table cooling recipe' as its own explicit line.

initial_information.value: Quality inspector on Line 2 day shift found crazing across the full width of two consecutive coils (HR-2050, HR-2051) following an unplanned rolling-speed reduction due to a downstream jam.

established_cause.value: Furnace temperature control and rolling-line speed control are on separate, non-integrated systems, so an unplanned speed change does not trigger a compensating temperature adjustment.

value: Manually reduce furnace zone temperatures for the remainder of the slowdown; scrap or downgrade the two affected coils per grade specification.

Implement an interim manual SOP requiring the line operator to notify the furnace operator within 60 seconds of any speed reduction event >15%, pending longer-term integration of the two control systems (tracked as a separate capital project).

initial_information.value: Recurring low-level crazing (under 0.5% of coils) reported by Line 1 across three consecutive weeks, always on the same roll stand, not tied to any single shift or grade.

established_cause.value: The stand-4 roll-change interval was extended for downtime reasons without validating that roll surface wear stays within tolerance over the new interval.

value: Revert stand-4 to the original 3-day roll-change interval immediately; inspect and replace current rolls.
Require any future roll-change interval modification to go through a documented wear-life validation (surface roughness measurement at proposed interval) and quality sign-off before implementation.

initial_information.value: Customer complaint received for coil HR-0998 (shipped 2 weeks prior) citing surface crazing discovered during their own downstream processing; internal inspection records for that coil show no defect was flagged at dispatch.

established_cause.value: Final inspection station lighting was specified for general defect visibility and was never updated to include the oblique/raking light angle needed to reliably detect fine crazing.

value: Notify the customer, arrange coil recall/credit per customer agreement; re-inspect recent shipments of the same grade under temporary raking-light setup.
Install adjustable-angle raking lighting at the final inspection station and add a documented crazing-specific inspection step to the final inspection SOP.

initial_information.value: Billet-cutting inspection on Caster 2 found visible non-metallic inclusions in the cross-section of 4 out of 40 billets sampled from heat H-3391.

established_cause.value: Refractory lining life is tracked manually with no automated or enforced trigger, so a lining can silently exceed its rated heat count before replacement.

value: Replace the tundish lining immediately; quarantine and section-test all billets cast on the current lining before further processing.
Move refractory life tracking into the caster's digital heat-count system with an automatic hold/alert when a lining approaches its rated heat count.

initial_information.value: Rolled coil from billets of heat H-3402 showed surface inclusions after hot rolling, traced back to the casting stage upon metallurgical review; affected roughly 8% of the heat's output.

established_cause.value: The quarterly slag-sensor calibration interval is too long relative to the sensor's actual drift rate, allowing detection sensitivity to degrade before recalibration.

value: Recalibrate the slag-detection sensor immediately; hold and re-sample billets from the affected heat.
Shorten the slag-detection sensor calibration interval from quarterly to monthly and add a mid-interval functional drift check using a reference standard.

initial_information.value: New grade trial heat H-3410 produced billets with inclusion levels above internal spec, discovered during first-article ultrasonic testing before the heat was released.

established_cause.value: The new-grade release process allows metallurgical approval and control-system recipe loading to proceed independently, with no system-enforced hold linking the two before a trial pour can begin.

value: Downgrade or scrap the affected trial heat per material disposition procedure; reload the correct recipe for any remaining trial pours.
Add a system interlock requiring confirmed recipe-load status before a trial heat can be initiated, sequencing metallurgy sign-off ahead of melt-shop release rather than in parallel.

initial_information.value: Routine metallurgical audit found elevated inclusion counts across multiple heats over a two-week period on Caster 1, none individually severe enough to trigger real-time rejection but trending upward.

established_cause.value: The ladle-treatment SOP specifies an argon flow target without explaining its purpose or acceptable deviation range, leaving operators to make undocumented adjustments without understanding the inclusion-control tradeoff.

value: Restore argon flow to the validated target setpoint on Caster 1 immediately; review recent heats for disposition.

Revise the ladle-treatment SOP to state the rationale for the argon flow target and its validated acceptable range, and add flow-rate logging with a supervisor alert for any sustained deviation beyond that range.

initial_information.value: A single severe inclusion cluster caused a billet to fracture during subsequent hot rolling on Line 2, halting production for 40 minutes; heat H-3425 traced as the source.

established_cause.value: The refractory incoming-inspection process can be bypassed under production time pressure because there is no system hold preventing unqualified stock from being pulled into use.

value: Halt use of the affected nozzle batch; complete incoming inspection on remaining units before any further use; disposition the fractured billet and downstream material.

Implement a physical/system lockout (e.g., barcode-gated storage) that prevents refractory stock from being issued to the floor until incoming inspection is marked complete, regardless of stock-out pressure.

initial_information.value: Irregular light-colored patches observed on the top surface of coil HR-2210, Line 3, covering roughly 10% of the coil's visible surface, first noticed mid-shift.

established_cause.value: Burner nozzle cleaning interval is set by shutdown-schedule convenience rather than by measured deposit-accumulation rate, allowing partial restriction to develop between cleanings.

value: Clean the affected burner nozzle immediately; inspect surrounding coils for similar patching.
Establish a deposit-accumulation-based cleaning interval (determined by periodic flow-rate testing) independent of shutdown scheduling, with interim manual flow checks between shutdowns.

initial_information.value: Line 1 day shift reported dull, irregular patches on coil HR-2260 concentrated near the strip centerline, coinciding with a recent descaler header maintenance.

established_cause.value: Descaler nozzle angle specifications exist in a separate engineering drawing that is not attached to or referenced by the maintenance work order, so correct reassembly depends on technician memory.

value: Re-angle the center-zone nozzle to specification immediately; re-inspect coils processed since the maintenance event.
Attach the nozzle-angle engineering drawing directly to the descaler maintenance work order template and require a photo-verification step confirming angle before sign-off.

initial_information.value: Sporadic patch defects (roughly 1 in 50 coils) reported across Line 2 over a month, with no single obvious cause identified by operators.

established_cause.value: Incoming slab inspection does not check surface oxide condition, a factor that trend data now implicates in patch defects, because the checklist was never revisited after initial design.

value: Add a surface oxide visual check to incoming inspection for the current slab lot; segregate slabs showing heavy oxide condition for closer monitoring.
Formally update the incoming slab inspection checklist to include a surface oxide condition rating, with a documented acceptance threshold agreed with both slab suppliers.

initial_information.value: Large single patch defect (approx. 0.3m x 0.2m) found on coil HR-2301, causing customer rejection at receiving inspection; traced to a localized event during rolling.

established_cause.value: There is no defined escalation threshold linking a logged 'degraded' maintenance observation to a mandatory corrective work order, so early warning signs are recorded but not acted on.

value: Service the refill valve immediately; issue customer credit/replacement per complaint procedure; inspect reservoir levels across all descaler stations.

Define explicit escalation thresholds in the maintenance logging system so that a 'degraded' rating on safety- or quality-critical components automatically generates a work order within a set timeframe.

initial_information.value: Night shift trainee flagged patch-like discoloration on coil HR-2318 but was unsure if it met the rejection threshold; coil was released and later reworked at customer's request.

established_cause.value: New visual defect-severity references are created centrally but there is no audit step ensuring they are physically deployed to every inspection station, so stations set up earlier remain without them.

value: Post laminated defect-severity reference photos at the Line 2 inspection station immediately; re-evaluate the released coil per customer agreement.
Add a quarterly audit checklist item confirming current visual reference materials are physically present and legible at every inspection station plant-wide.

initial_information.value: Multiple shallow pits visible on the top surface near the strip edge after descaling, batch HR-2291, Line 2 night shift, roughly 1 in 20 coils affected over two days.

established_cause.value: The maintenance scheduling system does not flag descaler nozzle cleaning as a hard-blocking task before shift handover, allowing it to be silently skipped under workload pressure.

value: Immediately inspect and clean all descaler header nozzles on Line 2; quarantine and re-inspect all coils produced since the start of the affected shift window before release.

Convert descaler nozzle inspection/cleaning into a hard-blocking checklist item in the shift-handover system that cannot be bypassed without supervisor sign-off; add a spray-pressure sensor alarm on the descaler header to flag a >=10% pressure drop in real time.

initial_information.value: Rolled pit defects observed on coil CR-0410, isolated to a 2m section, coinciding with a work-roll change earlier in the shift.

established_cause.value: The roll storage procedure predates the plant's current longer roll-inventory cycles and was never updated to require corrosion protection for rolls held longer than the original 48-hour assumption.

value: Remove and inspect the current work roll; replace with a roll confirmed free of surface pitting; disposition the affected 2m section.
Update the roll storage procedure to mandate corrosion-protective covering and a maximum uncovered storage duration, with a pre-installation surface inspection step for any roll stored over 7 days.

initial_information.value: Pitting defect cluster found during in-process inspection on Line 4, associated with a change to a new coolant supplier three weeks prior.

established_cause.value: The supplier-change approval process for rolling coolant does not include a required corrosion-inhibitor equivalence test, so relevant formulation differences can pass approval unnoticed.

value: Revert to the previous coolant supplier or formulation while the new one is re-evaluated; inspect and disposition affected coils from the last 3 weeks.
Add a mandatory corrosion-inhibitor equivalence test to the consumable supplier-change approval checklist for any coolant/lubricant substitution.

initial_information.value: Isolated pitting found on coil CR-0455 traced to a single roll bite event; equipment logs show a momentary tension drop at the same timestamp.

established_cause.value: The tension sensor cable lacks strain relief in a high-vibration routing zone, allowing the connector to loosen gradually until it caused an intermittent signal dropout.

value: Secure/replace the loose connector immediately; inspect the affected coil section and disposition per spec.
Add strain-relief hardware to the tension sensor cable routing and include cable connector integrity as a check item in the preventive maintenance schedule for that zone.

initial_information.value: Cluster of pitting defects found plant-wide across multiple lines over a single week, coinciding with an announced water-treatment plant maintenance event.

established_cause.value: There is no formal notification protocol requiring the utilities/water-treatment team to alert production quality before planned maintenance that could affect shared process inputs such as water pH.

value: Restore process water to spec; inspect and disposition affected production across all lines from the maintenance window.

Establish a formal cross-functional notification protocol requiring utilities to notify production quality at least 24 hours before any planned maintenance affecting shared process inputs, with a defined escalation contact.

initial_information.value: Embedded scale pattern found across the width of coil HR-2410, Line 1, first noticed at final visual inspection; no in-process alarm triggered.

established_cause.value: The descaler control system defaults to whatever state it was last left in rather than fail-safing to active, so a standby setting from a prior grade silently carries over to the next run.

value: Re-enable the descaler immediately; quarantine and downgrade the affected coil.
Reconfigure the descaler control logic to default to active at the start of every new coil/heat, requiring explicit operator confirmation to enter standby rather than to exit it.

initial_information.value: Localized rolled-in scale patches on coil HR-2455, appearing intermittently rather than continuously, Line 3.

established_cause.value: The preventive maintenance plan lacks a service-life-based replacement schedule for descaler pressure regulators, so aging units are only addressed reactively after failure symptoms appear.

value: Replace the aging pressure regulator immediately; inspect recent coils for intermittent scale patterns.
Add descaler pressure regulators to the PM plan with a proactive, service-life-based replacement schedule per manufacturer recommendation, rather than run-to-failure.

initial_information.value: Coil HR-2470 showed rolled-in scale concentrated at the leading edge only, Line 2 morning shift, first coil after a cold start following a weekend shutdown.

established_cause.value: The startup checklist sequences descaler pump activation after strip threading (to conserve water during idle time), which does not allow enough lead time for the pump to reach operating pressure before the leading edge passes through.

value: Trim and downgrade the affected leading-edge section; re-sequence remaining startup for this shift to pre-start the descaler.
Revise the startup checklist to activate the descaler pump a defined lead time (based on measured pressure ramp-up) before strip threading begins, accepting the minor water-usage tradeoff.

initial_information.value: Scale defect found on a single coil (HR-2481) traced to an operator manually bypassing the descaler for a rush order to save cycle time.

established_cause.value: The descaler bypass control, intended only for maintenance testing, was never access-restricted or logged, making it available for unauthorized production-floor use under schedule pressure.

value: Downgrade or scrap the affected coil; counsel the operator per standard practice and communicate the schedule-pressure concern to supervision for resolution.
Restrict the descaler bypass function to supervisor-level access with mandatory system logging of every activation, including a required reason code.

initial_information.value: Low-level rolled-in scale (isolated spots, not continuous) found sporadically across Line 1 over two months, no clear correlation with shift, grade, or equipment identified by initial investigation.

established_cause.value: Equipment upgrades (descaler nozzles) and utility specifications (water filtration mesh size) are managed by separate teams with no cross-check step at upgrade time, so filtration was never matched to the finer nozzle tolerances introduced years ago.

value: Add an interim finer in-line filter ahead of the descaler header on Line 1; flush and inspect current nozzles for partial clogs.
Establish a cross-functional sign-off requirement between equipment engineering and utilities whenever nozzle/spray equipment is upgraded, explicitly checking upstream filtration compatibility.

initial_information.value: Linear scratches found on multiple coils during final packaging inspection, Line 2, all oriented the same direction consistent with handling equipment contact.

established_cause.value: Transfer roller sleeve inspection is tracked on a manual paper sheet outside the digital maintenance system, so missed inspections are not visible on the compliance dashboard and go unnoticed.

value: Replace the worn roller sleeve immediately; inspect coils processed since the sleeve wear likely began.
Migrate transfer roller sleeve inspection into the digital maintenance tracking system with the same missed-task alerting used for other critical PM items.

initial_information.value: Single deep scratch found on coil FN-0512 during customer receiving inspection; internal records show no defect flagged before shipment.

established_cause.value: There is no formal reporting channel for loading-dock crew to flag equipment condition concerns to maintenance, so informally-raised issues (like sling padding wear) are not tracked or actioned.

value: Replace the sling padding immediately; process the customer complaint per procedure (credit/replacement); inspect other slings plant-wide.
Create a simple formal reporting channel (e.g., a logged tag-out or digital form) for floor/dock staff to flag equipment condition concerns, feeding directly into the maintenance work-order queue.

initial_information.value: Recurring fine scratches noted by quality on Line 4 across a shift, all short and randomly oriented, not matching any single equipment contact point.

established_cause.value: The finishing line cleaning SOP was written for single-shift operation and was never revisited when the plant moved to continuous 3-shift operation, since SOPs are only updated reactively after an incident, not proactively when operations change.

value: Perform an immediate mid-shift cleaning of contact surfaces on Line 4; inspect coils processed since the last cleaning.

Revise the cleaning SOP to include mid-shift cleaning cycles matched to the current 3-shift operating pattern, and add a trigger requiring SOP review whenever operating patterns (shift structure, line speed, etc.) change.

initial_information.value: Scratches found concentrated on the underside of coils only, Line 3, coinciding with the introduction of a new coil-turning device two weeks prior.

established_cause.value: Equipment procurement specifications were based on historical product mix without a required check against the current/forecasted product mix, so contact pads suited to thicker gauge were installed for a plant now running thinner gauges more often.

value: Replace the turning device contact pads with a gauge-appropriate variant; inspect coils processed since installation.
Add a mandatory current/forecasted product-mix review step to the equipment procurement checklist for any component specified against product dimensions.

initial_information.value: Isolated scratch complaint from a single customer order, traced to in-transit handling rather than plant-internal cause, following root-cause review with the logistics partner.

established_cause.value: Shipping and packaging instructions are distributed only via email to the internal logistics coordinator, with no requirement that they be physically posted at the loading bay where third-party carrier crews, who may lack email access, actually load the product.

value: Process the customer complaint per procedure; notify the logistics partner of the gap for this shipment and confirm corrective packaging on any remaining order quantity.

Require a printed/posted copy of shipping and packaging instructions at the physical loading bay for every order, verified by the logistics coordinator before loading begins, independent of the digital record.

initial_information.value: Half-circle-shaped material loss defect found at the trailing edge of sheared sheets from Line 4 shear station, roughly 1 in 30 sheets affected over the shift.

established_cause.value: The shear maintenance SOP has no periodic blade-position rotation step, so long runs at a single cut length concentrate blade wear at one contact point rather than distributing it across the blade.

value: Rotate or replace the shear blade at the worn position immediately; inspect and disposition affected sheets from the current run.
Add a periodic blade-position rotation step to the shear maintenance SOP, triggered by cumulative cut count at a fixed length rather than calendar time alone.

initial_information.value: Crescent gap defects appeared suddenly on Line 4 shear after a blade replacement earlier in the shift, affecting the first several sheets post-replacement.

established_cause.value: There is no formal process for removing or red-tagging obsolete alignment gauges when replacement tooling is introduced, so a superseded gauge remained available in the toolbox and was used by mistake.

value: Re-align the blade using the correct current gauge; inspect and disposition the affected first-run sheets.
Implement a formal red-tag/removal process for obsolete tooling whenever a replacement is introduced, with toolbox audits to confirm only current-generation tools remain accessible.

initial_information.value: Gradually worsening crescent gap severity noted across a full week on Line 4, not tied to any single maintenance event.

established_cause.value: Standard non-locking fasteners at the shear blade mount were specified under an older, lower cycle-rate assumption and were never upgraded to vibration-resistant hardware when the plant's shear cycle rate increased.

value: Re-torque blade mounting bolts to spec immediately; inspect and disposition affected sheets from the degrading-severity window.
Upgrade shear blade mount fasteners to vibration-resistant (e.g., nylon-insert or spring-lock) hardware rated for the current cycle rate, and add bolt-torque verification to the PM schedule.

initial_information.value: New operator on Line 4 produced a batch of sheets with crescent gap defects during their first solo shift on the shear station.

established_cause.value: The shear operator training curriculum was developed when the plant ran a narrower range of material thicknesses and under-emphasizes thickness-dependent blade gap adjustment; it was never revised as thickness variety in the product mix increased.

value: Correct the blade gap setting for the current material; inspect and disposition the affected batch; have a qualified operator review the remainder of the shift's output.

Revise the shear operator training curriculum to give thickness-dependent gap adjustment equal emphasis to length setting, including a hands-on competency check across at least 3 representative thicknesses before solo certification.

initial_information.value: Crescent gap defects found only on sheets from a specific coil (source coil CR-0620), not on adjacent coils processed on the same shear the same day.

established_cause.value: The metallurgical quality tracking system and the shop-floor coil tracking system are not integrated, so an upstream hardness deviation flag did not automatically follow the coil ID forward to the shear station, where it would have prompted a gap-setting adjustment.

value: Isolate and disposition remaining material from the flagged coil; adjust shear gap setting appropriately if the coil is still to be processed.

Integrate the metallurgical quality tracking system with the shop-floor coil tracking system (or implement an interim manual flag-transfer step) so upstream quality deviations are visible at every downstream operation referencing that coil ID.

initial_information.value: Visible folds/wrinkles found at the waist section of forged components from Press 2, affecting roughly 5% of the day's output, associated with a recent die change.

established_cause.value: Die drawing revisions and forging process parameter validation are approved through separate, unlinked workflows, so a geometry change like fillet radius does not automatically trigger re-validation of the forging parameters that depend on it.

value: Revert to the previous validated die or adjust forging parameters for the new fillet radius; disposition affected components.
Link the die drawing revision approval workflow to a mandatory forging-parameter re-validation step whenever die geometry changes, before the new die is released to production.

initial_information.value: Waist folding defects appeared intermittently on Press 3 across a shift, with severity varying part to part rather than being consistent.

established_cause.value: The induction heater's condition monitoring only tracks total output power, not zone-by-zone temperature uniformity, so a localized insulation breakdown in one coil section goes undetected as long as overall power output appears normal.

value: Repair or replace the affected induction coil section; inspect and disposition parts forged during the degraded-uniformity period.
Upgrade induction heater condition monitoring to include zone-by-zone temperature measurement (e.g., multi-point pyrometry) rather than relying on total output power alone.

initial_information.value: A batch of components from Press 2 showed waist folding traced to an incorrect billet size being fed into the press.

established_cause.value: The billet staging area lacks size-specific segregation because updating the physical layout requires a slow capital-request process, so mixed staging has persisted as an informal workaround even as the plant's product variant count grew.

value: Sort and segregate the current staging area by billet size immediately; inspect and disposition the affected batch.

Implement a low-cost interim segregation measure (labeled bins/floor markings) for billet staging pending the longer-term capital-approved layout change, with a written procedure requiring segregated staging regardless of layout constraints.

initial_information.value: Waist folding severity increased noticeably after a recent press-speed increase intended to improve throughput on Press 1.

established_cause.value: The throughput-improvement project approval template does not require a forming-quality impact assessment, so process speed changes can be approved based only on cycle-time and equipment-capability criteria, without checking their effect on material flow and defect risk.

value: Reduce press speed back toward the previous validated rate; disposition affected components produced at the higher speed.
Add a mandatory forming-quality impact assessment (including die-fill simulation or trial-run defect-rate check) to the throughput-improvement project approval template for any process speed change.

initial_information.value: Waist folding found on parts forged using a lubricant lot that was recently changed due to a supplier shortage, Press 3.

established_cause.value: The material change approval process only accounts for planned substitutions with advance lead time; it has no defined expedited-but-controlled equivalence check for emergency shortage situations, so the substitute lubricant went into production without a formal check.

value: Revert to the original lubricant if available, or perform an expedited friction/flow check on the substitute before continued use; disposition affected components.

Define an expedited (e.g., 24-48 hour) equivalence-check path within the material change approval process specifically for emergency shortage substitutions, covering the minimum critical properties (friction/flow for lubricants) rather than skipping evaluation entirely.

initial_information.value: Incomplete fusion detected at a coil-to-coil weld joint during continuous line processing, causing an unplanned line stop when the joint failed under tension, Line 1.

established_cause.value: The coil-welding station is not included on the standard gauge-range-change notification list used to update process parameters elsewhere in the plant, so its weld recipe was not updated for the new thinner gauge range.

value: Update the welder parameter recipe for the current gauge range immediately; inspect welds made since the gauge range change for fusion quality.

Add the coil-welding station to the standard gauge-range-change notification list, with a required parameter recipe update and verification weld test before resuming production after any gauge-range change.

initial_information.value: Weld joint offset (misalignment) detected downstream during rolling, causing localized thickness variation and downgrade of the affected section, Line 2.

established_cause.value: The automatic edge-alignment guide fault was classified as low-priority based on an assumption that manual alignment was an acceptable interim workaround, without verifying that manual alignment could actually meet the same tolerance as the automatic guide.

value: Repair the automatic edge-alignment guide; downgrade the affected section per thickness-variation spec; re-verify alignment on subsequent welds until repair is complete.
Require fault-priority classification for alignment-critical equipment to include a documented tolerance comparison against the proposed manual workaround before being downgraded to low-priority.

initial_information.value: Weld joint thickness variation exceeded spec on a joint made during a shift-change handover, Line 1.

established_cause.value: The welding station's shift-handover checklist is a generic equipment-status template that was never customized to include weld-parameter confirmation, a step specifically needed for this parameter-sensitive station.

value: Re-set weld pressure to the correct recipe value; disposition the affected joint's downstream material.
Customize the welding station's shift-handover checklist to include explicit weld-parameter confirmation (pressure, current, timing) in addition to general equipment status.

initial_information.value: Weld defect found during scheduled destructive testing of a sample joint, not causing a line stop but indicating a systemic quality drift over the past month's welds.

established_cause.value: The weld electrode replacement schedule is based on a wear-life study conducted on a single reference gauge that was never re-validated as the plant's product gauge-range variety expanded, so the fixed cycle-count assumption no longer matches actual wear across the current gauge range.

value: Inspect and replace electrodes showing wear beyond tolerance immediately; expand destructive-test sampling temporarily to characterize the current drift extent.
Re-validate the electrode wear-life study across the plant's current full gauge range and set a gauge-range-adjusted replacement schedule rather than a single fixed cycle count.

initial_information.value: Weld joint failure occurred shortly after a planned welder maintenance event, Line 2, first joint of the shift after restart.

established_cause.value: The welder maintenance work instruction was adopted directly from the equipment vendor's generic version without adding a plant-specific step to back up custom weld parameters before performing a controller reset, so resets silently revert to factory defaults.

value: Restore the correct weld parameter recipe immediately; inspect and disposition the failed joint and downstream material.
Add a mandatory parameter-backup step to the welder maintenance work instruction before any controller reset, plus a post-maintenance parameter-verification check before resuming production.

initial_information.value: Low-contrast staining found on finished coil FN-0601 surface, initially misidentified as oil spot during inspection before being confirmed as water spot via lab analysis.

established_cause.value: The drying unit's control system reports only an averaged temperature across all heater elements, masking a single failed element as a small overall deviation rather than surfacing it as a distinct fault.

value: Replace the failed heater element immediately; re-dry or disposition affected coils.
Upgrade the drying unit's control system to monitor and report per-element status, with an alarm for any individual element reading outside expected range regardless of the averaged total.

initial_information.value: Oil spot staining found on coil FN-0615, traced to residual rolling lubricant not fully removed during the cleaning stage prior to finishing.

established_cause.value: There is no defined process for forwarding chemical supplier reformulation notices from procurement to process engineering, so the cleaning solution replenishment system's calibration was not updated after a supplier reformulation changed the concentration profile.

value: Recalibrate the concentration-replenishment system to the new solution profile immediately; re-clean or disposition affected coils.

Establish a defined process requiring procurement to forward all supplier reformulation notices for process chemicals to process engineering, with a required calibration review within a set timeframe of receipt.

initial_information.value: Intermittent water spot staining on Line 2 finishing, correlating loosely with humid ambient conditions on certain days.

established_cause.value: The drying equipment was specified with a fixed time/temperature recipe because ambient humidity variation was not identified as a risk factor during the original equipment design, so the system has no way to compensate on high-humidity days.

value: Manually extend drying duration on days with elevated ambient humidity per a temporary supervisor-directed adjustment; inspect coils processed on recent humid days.

Evaluate and, if justified, retrofit humidity-adaptive drying control (e.g., a humidity sensor feeding an adjustable duration/temperature setpoint); in the interim, formalize the humidity-based manual adjustment as a documented procedure rather than an ad hoc supervisor call.

initial_information.value: Oil spot found concentrated near the coil core (innermost wraps) rather than distributed across the coil, Line 3.

established_cause.value: The wiper roll pneumatic cylinder's seals are only inspected reactively once a leak becomes obviously noticeable, rather than on a scheduled preventive interval, allowing a slow leak to develop and gradually reduce wiping pressure undetected.

value: Replace the pneumatic cylinder seals immediately; re-clean or disposition affected coil core sections.
Add wiper roll pneumatic cylinder seal replacement to the scheduled preventive maintenance plan at the manufacturer-recommended interval, rather than relying on reactive leak detection.

initial_information.value: Customer complaint received citing water spot staining discovered after the customer's own storage period; internal shipment inspection had passed the coil.

established_cause.value: There is no process linking changes in customer-facing storage/warranty terms to a required review of underlying manufacturing process specifications, so the drying process's visible-dryness-only target was never updated to a stricter moisture-content threshold when extended storage terms began being offered to customers.

value: Process the customer complaint per procedure; test recent shipments' moisture content against a newly-established threshold and disposition as needed.

Establish a defined moisture-content threshold for drying validation (not just visible dryness) calibrated to the longest storage period offered in current sales terms, and add a review trigger requiring process specification review whenever customer-facing storage/warranty terms change.

initial_information.value: Line 2 afternoon shift: fine surface cracking found on coil HR-2530, coinciding with the first coil run after a planned furnace refractory repair.

established_cause.value: The furnace refractory repair procedure does not require the patch material's thermal conductivity to match the original lining, allowing a mismatched patch to create an undetected local hot spot after repair.

value: Identify and correct the hot-spot zone temperature; downgrade the affected coil.
Add a thermal-conductivity matching requirement to the refractory repair procedure, with a post-repair thermal scan before the furnace is released to production.

initial_information.value: Line 1 night shift: crazing found on coil HR-2545, correlating with a recent change in incoming slab supplier for this grade.

established_cause.value: The slab supplier qualification process only reviews final chemistry and dimensions, not upstream casting process parameters like cooling rate, so a grain-structure difference relevant to thermal cracking susceptibility went unnoticed at qualification.

value: Adjust rolling temperature profile for the new supplier's slab characteristics; disposition affected coils.
Expand the slab supplier qualification checklist to request and review casting cooling-rate data, with a trial-run crazing-susceptibility check for any new supplier before full qualification.

initial_information.value: Caster 2: inclusion found in billet from heat H-3480, coinciding with an unusually long pour time due to a partial nozzle clog that was cleared mid-pour rather than stopping the heat.

established_cause.value: There is no documented threshold defining how long a partial nozzle clog can be tolerated before a pour must be stopped, leaving continuation decisions to operator judgment without a quality-risk basis.

value: Section-test the affected billets; disposition per inclusion findings.
Establish a documented maximum pour-time-extension threshold for partial nozzle clogs, beyond which the heat must be stopped and the nozzle cleared before continuing.

initial_information.value: Caster 1: inclusion cluster found in a billet from heat H-3495, traced to a batch of alloying wire with an unusually high moisture content from prolonged outdoor storage before use.

established_cause.value: The material storage plan lacks an overflow protocol for moisture-sensitive consumables when the climate-controlled store is full, so an over-capacity delivery of alloying wire defaulted to unprotected outdoor storage.

value: Discard or dry-recondition the affected wire batch per supplier guidance; disposition the affected billet.

Define a moisture-sensitive-consumable overflow protocol (e.g., temporary sealed containers, priority reordering to avoid overflow) for use whenever the primary climate-controlled store reaches capacity.

initial_information.value: Line 3: patches found on coil HR-2620, coinciding with a first-time production run using a newly commissioned furnace burner control algorithm update.

established_cause.value: The furnace control algorithm deployment process follows general IT software change management, which does not require a limited-scope live production trial before full rollout — a validation step process-control changes specifically need.

value: Revert to the previous algorithm version pending further validation; disposition affected coils.
Add a mandatory limited-scope live trial (e.g., single shift, single line) requirement to the furnace control algorithm deployment process before full rollout.

initial_information.value: Line 1: patches found on coil HR-2650, traced to uneven cooling from a partially blocked run-out table cooling header.

established_cause.value: Equipment specifications for water-contact components (like cooling headers) use generic industry-default water-quality assumptions instead of requiring the plant's actual measured water hardness as an input, resulting in under-designed scale resistance.

value: Clean the affected cooling header immediately; inspect and disposition affected coils.
Require site-specific water quality data (not generic defaults) as a mandatory input to the specification process for any new water-contact equipment.

initial_information.value: Line 4: pitting found on coil CR-0810, traced to a coolant tank that had not been fully drained and cleaned during a scheduled changeover to a new coolant chemistry.

established_cause.value: The coolant tank has physical drainage low points that the standard drain valve doesn't reach, and the changeover procedure was never updated to include a supplementary manual removal step for the resulting residual fluid.

value: Fully drain, manually clean, and refill the tank with correct-chemistry coolant; disposition affected coils.
Add a supplementary manual residual-fluid removal step to the coolant changeover procedure, specifically addressing the tank's known drainage low points.

initial_information.value: Line 3: pitting found on coil CR-0845, coinciding with an extended weekend idle period during which the line was not run.

established_cause.value: The idle-equipment protection procedure has thresholds for overnight and 7+ day stoppages but no coverage for the 2-3 day weekend-length gap in between, so rolls sitting idle over a weekend receive no anti-corrosion protection.

value: Clean and inspect the affected work rolls; disposition affected coils.
Add a weekend/2-3-day idle threshold to the idle-equipment protection procedure, requiring anti-corrosion coating application for any stoppage beyond the standard overnight duration.

initial_information.value: Line 2: rolled-in scale found on coil HR-2710, coinciding with a temporary reduction in furnace excess-air ratio made to reduce fuel consumption.

established_cause.value: Energy-efficiency projects, including furnace atmosphere adjustments, are approved without a required cross-review from quality/process engineering, so downstream effects like more tenacious oxide scale formation are not checked before implementation.

value: Revert the excess-air ratio to the previous validated setting; inspect coils processed under the adjusted setting.
Require a quality/process engineering cross-review, specifically checking scale-formation and descaling impact, as part of the approval process for any furnace atmosphere or energy-efficiency change.

initial_information.value: Line 1: scale defect found on coil HR-2740, traced to a descaler water temperature that was colder than usual due to a seasonal ambient temperature drop.

established_cause.value: The descaler system was validated during commissioning using only summer-season water temperature data, and this validation was never repeated across a full seasonal cycle, so its performance at winter water temperatures was never actually verified until this defect occurred.

value: Increase descaler pressure/pass count temporarily to compensate for colder water; inspect affected coils.
Perform a full seasonal-cycle validation of descaler performance, and if winter performance is confirmed inadequate, add a water pre-heating step or a seasonally-adjusted pressure recipe.

initial_information.value: Line 2: scratches found on coil FN-0720, traced to a recently installed automated coil-wrapping machine's guide arm making unintended contact.

established_cause.value: The equipment commissioning checklist used for this installation was a generic template not tailored to diameter-sensitive equipment, so testing across the full production coil-diameter range was never required before the machine was accepted into production.

value: Adjust or restrict the guide arm's motion path pending full validation; inspect coils processed since installation.

Create a diameter-range validation requirement in the commissioning checklist for any future diameter-sensitive equipment installation, testing across the plant's full production range before acceptance.

initial_information.value: Line 3: scratches found on coil FN-0755, traced to grit contamination on a conveyor belt from a nearby floor-grinding maintenance activity performed without adequate containment.

established_cause.value: The maintenance work permit template covers safety hazards but has no product-contamination risk category, so dust-generating maintenance work near active production lines is not automatically flagged for containment requirements.

value: Clean the affected conveyor and inspect/disposition the affected coil; halt the grinding work until containment is in place.

Add a product-contamination risk category to the maintenance work permit template, requiring containment measures for any dust/particulate-generating work within a defined proximity to active production equipment.

initial_information.value: Line 4 shear station: crescent gap defect found on sheets following a die-set change to a different shear blade set for a specialty order.

established_cause.value: Specialty tooling used infrequently for special orders was introduced outside the standard tooling calibration tracking process, so its calibration status is not visible or enforced the same way as regularly-used blade sets.

value: Calibrate the specialty blade set to the correct matched-pair spec immediately; inspect and disposition the affected sheets.
Integrate all specialty and infrequently-used tooling into the standard tooling calibration tracking system, regardless of usage frequency.

initial_information.value: Line 4 shear station: crescent gap defects found intermittently, correlating loosely with ambient temperature swings between day and night shift in a non-climate-controlled area of the plant.

established_cause.value: The blade clearance setup procedure treats clearance as fixed after initial setup, without accounting for ambient-temperature-driven frame expansion specific to this non-climate-controlled shear station location, so no mid-shift re-verification occurs.

value: Re-verify and adjust blade clearance now; inspect and disposition affected sheets from the temperature-swing period.
Add a mid-shift blade clearance re-verification step specifically for this shear station, or install a climate-controlled enclosure if a permanent fix is preferred.

initial_information.value: Press 1: waist folding found on components forged using a billet lot that had been in inventory significantly longer than typical before use.

established_cause.value: The billet inventory management system tracks weight and grade but not storage duration, so aged billets exceeding the recommended maximum storage time before use are not flagged and can be pulled for forging without extra oxide-removal preparation.

value: Apply additional surface preparation (extended descaling/preheat) to remaining aged billets in the lot before forging; disposition affected components.
Add a storage-duration aging flag to the billet inventory management system, triggering additional surface preparation steps for any billet exceeding the recommended maximum storage time.

initial_information.value: Press 2: waist folding found after switching to a new forging lubricant intended to reduce environmental impact, first batch using the new product.

established_cause.value: Sustainability-driven material substitutions are approved through an environmental/compliance pathway that does not require a forming-quality equivalence test from process/quality engineering, so a friction-performance gap in the new lubricant went unchecked before production use.

value: Revert to the previous lubricant or increase die lubrication frequency as an interim measure; disposition affected components.

Require a forming-quality equivalence test (friction/flow performance) from process/quality engineering as part of any sustainability-driven material substitution approval, in addition to environmental/compliance criteria.

initial_information.value: Line 2 coil welder: weld defect found coinciding with a recent replacement of the welder's electrode material with a different manufacturer's equivalent-spec electrode.

established_cause.value: The consumable substitution approval process assumes that a nominal specification match between electrode suppliers guarantees equivalent real-world performance, without requiring an in-process verification weld test before the substitution goes into production use.

value: Adjust weld parameters to compensate for the new electrode's actual resistivity, or revert to the previous supplier; disposition affected joints.
Require an in-process verification weld test (not just spec-sheet comparison) before approving any welding consumable substitution, regardless of nominal specification match.

initial_information.value: Line 1 coil welder: weld joint thickness variation found, traced to a slight but persistent voltage fluctuation in the plant's electrical supply during a specific time window each day.

established_cause.value: Electrical installation planning for new equipment groups circuits by physical proximity rather than power-quality sensitivity, so the coil welder — which is sensitive to voltage fluctuation — was never given a dedicated, conditioned power circuit.

value: Adjust weld schedule to avoid the known voltage-fluctuation window as an interim measure; disposition affected joints from the recurring window.

Install a dedicated, conditioned power circuit for the coil welder, and add power-quality sensitivity as a required consideration in future electrical installation planning for parameter-sensitive equipment.

initial_information.value: Line 3 finishing: water spot staining found on coils processed during a period when the plant's compressed air supply (used for final surface blow-off before drying) had noticeably higher moisture content.

established_cause.value: Compressed air dryer maintenance is scheduled purely on a calendar basis without a moisture-level indicator check, so desiccant saturation driven by variable plant-wide air demand goes undetected until it affects moisture-sensitive downstream processes like finishing blow-off.

value: Regenerate/replace the dryer desiccant immediately; re-dry or disposition affected coils.
Add a moisture-level indicator (e.g., dew-point sensor) to the compressed air dryer with an alert threshold, supplementing the calendar-based maintenance schedule rather than replacing it.

initial_information.value: Line 2 finishing: oil spot found on a coil, traced to a hydraulic fluid micro-leak on an overhead crane used in the finishing area, dripping onto coils during transit below.

established_cause.value: The overhead crane inspection procedure, adapted from a general safety-focused checklist, does not require elevated close-up inspection of hydraulic fittings specifically to catch leaks that could drip contamination onto product moving below.

value: Repair the leaking fitting immediately; inspect and disposition coils that may have been under the crane's travel path during the leak period.

Add a scheduled elevated close-up hydraulic fitting inspection (not just ground-level visual) to the overhead crane maintenance procedure, specifically for cranes operating above product-handling areas.

initial_information.value: Line 4 finishing: water spot staining found only on coils processed directly after the drying unit's exhaust fan was temporarily run at reduced speed to address a noise complaint.

established_cause.value: The noise-complaint response procedure treats all equipment the same regardless of process criticality, so a drying-unit exhaust fan (whose speed directly affects product moisture removal) was adjusted for noise reduction without any required production/quality sign-off on the process impact.

value: Restore the exhaust fan to its validated operating speed; identify an alternative noise-mitigation approach; re-dry or disposition affected coils.
Add a process-criticality flag to equipment records, requiring production/quality sign-off before any noise- or comfort-driven adjustment to process-critical equipment like drying unit exhaust fans.

initial_information.value: Line 3 finishing: oil spot found concentrated at coil wrap transitions, traced to a slight over-application of anti-corrosion oil by an automated oiling system following a nozzle recalibration.

established_cause.value: The oiling system recalibration checklist assumes the technician will use the current production width as the reference target without an explicit prompt to confirm it, allowing recalibration against a mismatched width and resulting in incorrect flow rate.

value: Recalibrate the nozzle flow rate for the current production width; re-clean or disposition affected coils.
Add an explicit current-production-width confirmation step to the oiling system recalibration checklist before flow rate adjustment.

initial_information.value: Line 3: crazing found on coil HR-2810, coinciding with a period when the plant's compressed nitrogen supply (used for furnace atmosphere control on this grade) was running at reduced purity due to a supplier quality issue.

established_cause.value: Incoming inspection for bulk gas deliveries checks only quantity and pressure, with no required review of the supplier's purity certificate against the plant's minimum specification before the gas is used in production.

value: Quarantine the current nitrogen supply pending purity verification; disposition affected coils.
Add a mandatory purity-certificate review step to incoming inspection for all bulk gas deliveries used in atmosphere-controlled processes.

initial_information.value: Line 2: crazing found on coil HR-2835, traced to a furnace zone thermocouple that had drifted out of calibration, reading lower than actual temperature.

established_cause.value: The thermocouple calibration interval is based on generic manufacturer guidance rather than validated against this furnace's actual observed drift rate, allowing significant drift to develop mid-cycle before the next scheduled calibration catches it.

value: Recalibrate the affected thermocouple immediately; verify and correct actual furnace temperature; disposition affected coils.
Perform a drift-rate study for this furnace's thermocouples and set a calibration interval based on the actual observed drift rate rather than generic guidance, shortening the interval if warranted.

initial_information.value: Caster 2: inclusion found in billet from heat H-3520, coinciding with a first-time use of a new tundish design intended to improve throughput.

established_cause.value: The tundish design approval process for throughput-improvement projects does not include a required inclusion-cleanliness (float-out time) impact assessment, so a shorter melt residence time's effect on inclusion removal was not evaluated before deployment.

value: Revert to the previous tundish design pending further evaluation; section-test billets cast with the new design.
Add a required inclusion-cleanliness impact assessment (e.g., a trial-heat inclusion count comparison) to the tundish design approval process for any future throughput-improvement changes.

initial_information.value: Caster 1: inclusion found in billet from heat H-3535, traced to a ladle slide-gate mechanism that was sticking intermittently, causing uneven flow control during pouring.

established_cause.value: The slide-gate mechanism's cleaning schedule was set once at commissioning based on assumed deposit accumulation and has never been revisited against actual observed in-service sticking patterns, allowing real-world deposit buildup to outpace the fixed schedule.

value: Clean and service the slide-gate mechanism immediately; section-test the affected billets.
Revise the slide-gate cleaning schedule based on actual observed friction/sticking data rather than the original commissioning-time assumption, with periodic re-validation.

initial_information.value: Line 3: patches found on coil HR-2910, traced to a recently repaired furnace door seal that was not restoring full seal pressure, allowing localized cold air infiltration.

established_cause.value: The furnace door seal repair procedure only addresses gasket replacement and assumes that's the sole failure mode, so it has no step to verify door alignment — meaning gradual alignment drift goes uncorrected even when the gasket itself is repaired.

value: Re-align the furnace door and re-verify seal contact; disposition affected coils.
Add a door alignment verification step to the seal repair procedure, performed alongside every gasket replacement.

initial_information.value: Line 1: patches found on coil HR-2945, coinciding with a first production run after annual furnace refractory relining.

established_cause.value: The refractory cure-time procedure is based on the manufacturer's generic guidance assuming a standard heat-up ramp rate, without site-specific validation of this furnace's actual (slower) ramp-up characteristics, so the cure window ends before the lining is actually fully cured.

value: Hold production and complete the full cure cycle based on actual measured temperature, not elapsed time alone; disposition affected coils.
Validate this furnace's actual ramp-up rate and set cure completion criteria based on measured temperature achievement, not generic elapsed time, for all future relines.

initial_information.value: Line 4: pitting found on coil CR-0910, traced to a coolant pH drift caused by a delayed response to a routine pH test result showing early signs of drift.

established_cause.value: The coolant pH testing procedure has a target range but no escalation trigger for results trending toward the edge of it, so early drift warnings sit unaddressed until the next scheduled weekly review rather than prompting immediate action.

value: Correct coolant pH to target range immediately; disposition affected coils from the drift period.

Add a trend-based escalation trigger to the pH testing procedure (e.g., two consecutive readings moving toward the range edge trigger immediate corrective dosing), rather than waiting for the weekly review.

initial_information.value: Line 3: pitting found on coil CR-0945, traced to a batch of work rolls that had been reground by an external contractor using a different roughness specification than the plant's standard.

established_cause.value: The work order for external roll regrinding references the roughness specification by an internal document number rather than including the actual numeric values, and the external contractor has no access to that internal document, so they defaulted to their own standard.

value: Re-grind or replace the affected rolls to correct specification; disposition affected coils.
Update the external regrinding work order template to include the actual roughness specification values directly, rather than referencing an internal document number the contractor cannot access.

initial_information.value: Line 2: scale defect found on coil HR-3010, traced to a descaler pump motor running at slightly reduced speed due to an aging variable-frequency drive (VFD).

established_cause.value: VFD maintenance only reacts to fault codes and includes no periodic performance-capability test, so gradual component degradation that reduces maximum motor output — without yet triggering an outright fault — goes undetected until it causes a downstream quality issue.

value: Replace or repair the degraded VFD; verify descaler pump reaches full rated speed; disposition affected coils.
Add a periodic performance-capability test (verifying actual maximum output against rated spec) to VFD preventive maintenance for all quality-critical drives, not just fault-code monitoring.

initial_information.value: Line 1: scale defect found on coil HR-3045, traced to a batch of slabs with unusually adherent scale characteristics linked to a specific chemistry variation within the approved grade tolerance.

established_cause.value: The descaler recipe was validated using only mid-tolerance reference chemistry rather than being tested across the full approved chemistry tolerance band, so material at the high-silicon end of tolerance — known to produce more adherent scale — was never confirmed to descale adequately at the standard setting.

value: Increase descaler pressure/pass count for the current high-silicon slab batch; disposition affected coils.
Re-validate the descaler recipe across the full chemistry tolerance band for this grade, establishing a chemistry-adjusted recipe if high-silicon material is confirmed to need different settings.

initial_information.value: Line 2: scratches found on coil FN-0820, traced to a temporary steel plate placed over a floor gap near the finishing line during an unrelated facilities repair, creating a sharp transition edge in the coil transport path.

established_cause.value: The facilities work request process checks safety and structural criteria but has no step requiring a check against active product-transport paths before installing temporary floor modifications near production lines.

value: Correct or remove the floor plate to restore a flush transition; inspect and disposition affected coils.
Add a product-transport-path check to the facilities work request process for any temporary or permanent floor modification near active production areas.

initial_information.value: Line 4: scratches found on coil FN-0855, traced to a slitting operation upstream of finishing where a slitter knife had a small chip, leaving a burr that scored subsequent wraps during coiling.

established_cause.value: The slitter knife selection guide is based on typical/average hardness for each grade rather than the full hardness tolerance range, so material at the harder end of the grade's tolerance can exceed the selected knife's capability and cause chipping.

value: Replace the chipped knife; inspect and disposition coils processed since the chip developed.
Revise the knife selection guide to account for the full hardness tolerance range within each grade, selecting knife hardness/type based on the upper tolerance bound rather than the typical value.

initial_information.value: Line 4 shear station: crescent gap found on sheets, traced to a shear hydraulic system pressure drop caused by a slow internal seal leak in the hydraulic cylinder.

established_cause.value: The hydraulic pressure monitoring point was chosen for ease of installation access rather than diagnostic completeness, so it reflects pump output pressure but cannot detect an internal seal leak occurring downstream at the cylinder.

value: Repair the cylinder seal; restore full system pressure; inspect and disposition affected sheets.
Add a second pressure monitoring point at or near the cylinder (point of use) to enable detection of downstream pressure loss that the pump-output sensor alone cannot catch.

initial_information.value: Line 4 shear station: crescent gap found on the first sheet of each run for several consecutive runs, but not on subsequent sheets within the same run.

established_cause.value: The run-start sequence was optimized purely for minimizing cycle time between runs, without a documented trade-off evaluation against the first-sheet defect risk created by not allowing hydraulic pressure to stabilize before the first cut.

value: Add a brief pressure-stabilization pause to the current run-start sequence; disposition affected first-sheets from recent runs.
Formally evaluate and document the cycle-time vs. defect-risk trade-off, setting a run-start hydraulic stabilization hold based on measured pressure ramp-up time.

initial_information.value: Press 1: waist folding found on components, traced to a die-cooling channel partially blocked by scale buildup, causing localized die surface temperature to run higher than intended.

established_cause.value: The die maintenance procedure's scope covers visible external wear surfaces but not internal cooling channels, so gradual debris accumulation inside the cooling passages — which affects die temperature control — is never addressed by routine maintenance.

value: Clear the blocked cooling channel; verify die surface temperature returns to spec; disposition affected components.
Expand the die maintenance procedure's scope to include periodic internal cooling channel inspection and cleaning, not just external wear surfaces.

initial_information.value: Press 2: waist folding found on components forged immediately following an operator shift change, first few parts of the new shift only.
